content.content:
1	=== detach-and-attach
2	     1	---
3	     2	title: Detach and Attach Audio
4	     3	description: Split a clip's sound onto a linked clip of its own, keep the two in step, and merge them back into one clip.
5	     4	---
6	     5	
7	     6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	     7	
9	     8	Detach Audio splits a clip's sound onto its own clip, so you can trim, move or process the sound apart from the picture. Attach Audio merges the two back into one clip.
10	     9	
11	    10	<AtAGlance
12	    11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
13	    12	  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
14	    13	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Mix"
15	    14	  tools={['detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'set_enabled']}
16	    15	/>
17	    16	
18	    17	## Detach audio
19	    18	
20	    19	Select one or more clips and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>. **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** and the **Detach Audio** button in the [Mix section](/audio/pan-and-mono/) of the Sound sub-tab do the same.
21	    20	
22	    21	Each selected clip splits in two, as one undo step:
23	    22	
24	    23	- The original clip keeps its picture, and its audio is switched off.
25	    24	- A new clip appears on the track directly below. It plays only sound, from the same file, with the same in point, length and speed, and it keeps the original's audio settings and actions.
26	    25	
27	    26	If the clip is already on the bottom track, Frame Job adds a new track underneath for the sound. Otherwise the sound always goes on the next track down, so make room there first, or drag the sound to another track afterwards.
28	    27	
29	    28	The two clips are now a **linked pair**. Trim the sound on its own to make a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
30	    29	
31	    30	### When Detach Audio won't work
32	    31	
33	    32	Frame Job beeps, changes nothing, and the inspector's foot says why:
34	    33	
35	    34	| The inspector's foot says | What it means |
36	    35	| --- | --- |
37	    36	| "…media 2 has no audio track" | The clip's file has no sound. |
38	    37	| "…its audio is switched off" | The clip has already been detached, or its sound is otherwise off. |
39	    38	| "…it is not a media clip" | The clip is text, a shape, a graphic, a picture, a freeze frame, a nest or an adjustment clip. |
40	    39	| "clips 4 and 7 would overlap by…, more than half of the shorter clip…" | The track below already has a clip where the sound would land. |
41	    40	| "clip 4 would overlap more than one neighbour on one side…" | The sound would reach more than one clip on the track below. |
42	    41	
43	    42	A smaller overlap with one clip on the track below is allowed, and it becomes a cross dissolve between the two.
44	    43	
45	    44	With several clips selected, the ones that can be detached are, and the rest are skipped. The inspector's foot only gives a reason when none of them could be.
46	    45	
47	    46	## See which clips are linked
48	    47	
49	    48	Each half of a linked pair shows a link symbol after its kind symbol, in the clip's name strip. Select one and the other gets a dashed ring in your Mac's accent colour, because edits to one move both. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/#linked-clips).
50	    49	
51	    50	### A clip with its audio off
52	    51	
53	    52	A clip whose audio is off shows no waveform and no fade handles. A clip with its picture and its sound both off is drawn dimmed. The picture half of a linked pair has no Sound sub-tab, so select the sound half to change anything about the sound.
54	    53	
55	    54	## What stays in sync
56	    55	
57	    56	A linked picture and sound stay in step in time through your edits.
58	    57	
59	    58	| Edit | What happens to the pair |
60	    59	| --- | --- |
61	    60	| Move | Moving either clip moves both by the same amount. Only the clip you drag changes track, so you can drag the sound to another track and its picture stays where it is. When a move would take either clip past the start of the timeline, both stop together. |
62	    61	| [Split](/editing/splitting/) | A split through both pairs the two halves on each side of the cut. When the cut only crosses one of the clips, the other stays linked to the piece it shares more time with, and the other piece loses its link. |
63	    62	| [Duplicate](/editing/duplicate-clips/), [Nest](/editing/nests/) and Ripple Delete | Take both clips. |
64	    63	| [Copy and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | A selected picture brings its sound, so the pair pastes as a pair. A selected sound is copied on its own, and the pasted copy isn't linked to anything. |
65	    64	| Ripple edits, [Close Gap and Insert Time](/editing/close-gaps/) | Move the other half too. |
66	    65	| [Trim and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone) | On the picture, the edit carries to the sound when their edges line up. On the sound, it moves the sound alone. |
67	    66	| [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) | Slips both, as far as the one with less room allows. |
68	    67	| Delete | Deleting the picture deletes its sound too. See [Remove a clip's sound](#remove-a-clips-sound). |
69	    68	| [Speed](/speed/change-speed/) and [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) | Frame Job won't do these on a linked clip. See [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed). |
70	    69	
71	    70	A ripple edit that would push a sound starting before its picture past the start of the timeline doesn't happen at all. The inspector's foot says the sound "would start before 0".
72	    71	
73	    72	Locks win over links. A partner on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track) isn't moved, split, trimmed, slipped, duplicated, nested or deleted with its clip. **Copy** is the exception: a selected picture brings its sound even from a locked track.
74	    73	
75	    74	## Remove a clip's sound
76	    75	
77	    76	Select the sound half and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. The picture stays, silent, and its link is gone. Detach Audio and then deleting the sound is how you drop a clip's sound for good.
78	    77	
79	    78	Undo brings the sound back. Once the sound clip is gone, no control in the app turns the picture's own audio back on.
80	    79	
81	    80	## Attach audio
82	    81	
83	    82	Select either half of a pair and press <kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Attach Audio**. The **Attach Audio** button in the Mix section does the same, but it's only there with the sound half selected, because the picture half has no Sound sub-tab.
84	    83	
85	    84	The picture's audio comes back on with the sound clip's audio settings, and the sound clip is removed. Its track stays, empty if nothing else is on it. With several pairs selected, each one merges, as one undo step.
86	    85	
87	    86	**Clip ▸ Attach Audio** is greyed out until the selection holds a linked clip.
88	    87	
89	    88	### When Attach Audio won't work
90	    89	
91	    90	The two halves have to match, because they're becoming one clip. They need the same start, length, in point and speed, and the same actions at the same times with the same curves. Otherwise the inspector's foot says "clip 4's picture and clip 5's sound do not cover the same time; trim them to match before Attach Audio". This is what a J-cut or an L-cut does on purpose. Trim the two to the same start and end first, and remove or match any action you added to only one half.
92	    91	
93	    92	## Actions and speed
94	    93	
95	    94	The new sound clip gets a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working. An action that only changes the picture does nothing on the sound clip. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/#detach-audio).
96	    95	
97	    96	A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) keeps it: the sound clip's copy of the Speed actions gives it the same ramp, so the two stay in step.
98	    97	
99	    98	Frame Job won't change the speed or direction of either half while they're linked, because the two would have to be re-timed identically. That covers Speed, Reverse, rate stretch, [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/), and adding, moving or changing a Speed action. The inspector's foot says "clip 4 is linked to clip 5: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction". Attach, make the change, then detach again.
100	    99	
101	   100	Attaching keeps the sound's work. The picture takes the sound clip's audio settings, and each of its actions takes the audio values of the sound clip's action at the same place.
102	   101	
103	   102	## With an agent
104	   103	
105	   104	`set_enabled` turns a clip's picture or sound on or off, which no control in the app does. After a detached sound has been deleted, it's the way to switch the picture's own audio back on. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).
106	   105	
107	   106	## Related
108	   107	
109	   108	- [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/)
110	   109	- [Pan and Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/)
111	   110	- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
112	   111	- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
113	=== j-and-l-cuts
114	     1	---
115	     2	title: J-cuts and L-cuts
116	     3	description: Let a shot's sound start before its picture, or run on under the next shot, by trimming the sound half of a linked pair.
117	     4	---
118	     5	
119	     6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
120	     7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
121	     8	
122	     9	A J-cut brings in the next shot's sound before its picture. An L-cut lets a shot's sound run on under the next shot. Both soften a cut, and in Frame Job both come from trimming the sound half of a [detached clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
123	    10	
124	    11	<AtAGlance
125	    12	  keys={['W', 'E']}
126	    13	  where={["Timeline: drag a detached sound clip's edge", 'Timeline: ⌥⇧-drag an edge to roll']}
127	    14	  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end', 'roll']}
128	    15	/>
129	    16	
130	    17	## Make a J-cut
131	    18	
132	    19	<Steps>
133	    20	
134	    21	1. Select the later shot and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd> to [detach its audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/#detach-audio).
135	    22	
136	    23	2. If the shot before it is detached too, drag this sound to a track of its own. See [Keep the sound off its neighbour](#keep-the-sound-off-its-neighbour).
137	    24	
138	    25	3. Drag the sound clip's start edge to the left.
139	    26	
140	    27	</Steps>
141	    28	
142	    29	The sound now begins before its picture. The picture stays where it is.
143	    30	
144	    31	## Make an L-cut
145	    32	
146	    33	<Steps>
147	    34	
148	    35	1. Select the earlier shot and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>.
149	    36	
150	    37	2. If the next shot's sound is on the track the sound went to, drag this sound to a track of its own.
151	    38	
152	    39	3. Drag the sound clip's end edge to the right.
153	    40	
154	    41	</Steps>
155	    42	
156	    43	The sound now runs on after its picture has ended.
157	    44	
158	    45	## Keep the sound off its neighbour
159	    46	
160	    47	When two neighbouring shots are both detached, their sounds sit side by side on one track. Lengthening one into the other overlaps them, and an overlap on a track is a [cross dissolve](/audio/crossfades/), not a split edit. On a track of its own, the sound overlaps nothing.
161	    48	
162	    49	## How far the sound can go
163	    50	
164	    51	A trim can only reveal what's in the file. The sound stops at the first or last frame of its media, and at the start of the timeline. Choose a shot with spare sound before its in point for a J-cut, or after its out point for an L-cut.
165	    52	
166	    53	The sound has to keep at least one frame. If it runs into another clip on its track, Frame Job allows an overlap of up to half the shorter clip and won't go further.
167	    54	
168	    55	## Trim and roll a sound clip alone
169	    56	
170	    57	The half you grab decides what moves. An edit on the sound moves only the sound. An edit on the picture also moves the sound when their edges line up. A lead you've already made isn't lined up, so trimming that picture's start leaves the sound alone.
171	    58	
172	    59	Dragging is what lengthens a sound. <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> [trim to the playhead](/editing/trimming/#trim-to-the-playhead), so they only shorten it, and they do it to the sound alone. To roll the cut between two sound clips on one track, hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the edge between them. A sound on a track of its own has no cut to roll.
173	    60	
174	    61	See [Move a sound clip's edge alone](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone).
175	    62	
176	    63	## Good to know
177	    64	
178	    65	- Moving either half keeps the lead. When a drag would take the sound past the start of the timeline, both clips stop together.
179	    66	- A ripple edit that would push a leading sound past the start of the timeline doesn't happen.
180	    67	- Frame Job won't [attach](/audio/detach-and-attach/#attach-audio) a pair that no longer covers the same time. Trim the two to the same start and end first.
181	    68	- [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) always takes both halves.
182	    69	
183	    70	## With an agent
184	    71	
185	    72	A person's trim on a sound moves it alone automatically. An agent has to ask for that, or a trim on a sound with an edge lined up with its picture moves both. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
186	    73	
187	    74	## Related
188	    75	
189	    76	- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
190	    77	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
191	    78	- [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
192	    79	- [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/)
193	=== mute-and-solo
194	     1	---
195	     2	title: Mute and solo tracks
196	     3	description: Silence a track, or hear only the tracks you pick, and see what that does to the picture, nests and an export.
197	     4	---
198	     5	
199	     6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
200	     7	
201	     8	Mute silences one track. Solo silences every other track, so you can hear one part of the mix by itself. Neither touches the picture.
202	     9	
203	    10	<AtAGlance
204	    11	  menu={['Track ▸ Mute Audio', 'Track ▸ Solo']}
205	    12	  where={['The speaker and headphones switches in the track header', "The track's right-click menu"]}
206	    13	  tools="set_track"
207	    14	/>
208	    15	
209	    16	## Mute a track
210	    17	
211	    18	Click the speaker switch in the track's header. Every clip on the track goes silent, and the picture is unaffected. Click it again to bring the sound back.
212	    19	
213	    20	**Mute Audio** in the track's right-click menu does the same for the track you clicked. **Track ▸ Mute Audio** acts on the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track): the track of the first selected clip, or the front track when nothing is selected.
214	    21	
215	    22	To silence one clip and not its whole track, use its own [**Mute**](/audio/volume/#mute-a-clip).
216	    23	
217	    24	## Solo a track
218	    25	
219	    26	Click the headphones switch in the track's header, or choose **Solo** in the track's right-click menu or the **Track** menu. Every other track in the same container goes silent. A container is the timeline, or one nest's own tracks.
220	    27	
221	    28	You can solo several tracks. All the soloed tracks play, and everything else in the container is silenced.
222	    29	
223	    30	**Solo** shows a checkmark in the **Track** menu while it's on. Neither **Solo** nor **Mute Audio** has a keyboard shortcut. Each flip is one undo step, "Mute Track" or "Solo Track".
224	    31	
225	    32	## How mute and solo combine
226	    33	
227	    34	- **Mute always wins.** A track that's both muted and soloed stays silent.
228	    35	- **Solo doesn't look at what's on the track.** A soloed track with nothing on it still silences the rest, as a mixer's solo button does.
229	    36	- **Pictures stay.** A silenced track still draws. To take a picture out, use [Hide Video](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#hide-video), which leaves the sound playing.
230	    37	
231	    38	## See what a solo silences
232	    39	
233	    40	Under a solo, the waveforms on silenced tracks draw faded, as they do on a muted track. Their speaker switches stay unlit, because a speaker shows that track's own setting and not what a solo is doing to it. So the waveform tells you what you'll hear, and the switch tells you what you've set.
234	    41	
235	    42	## Mute and solo in nests
236	    43	
237	    44	A solo only reaches tracks in its own container:
238	    45	
239	    46	- A solo on a timeline track silences the other timeline tracks, and a nest playing on one of them goes silent with it.
240	    47	- A solo on a track inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) affects only that nest's other tracks.
241	    48	
242	    49	Muting the track a nest clip sits on silences everything inside the nest. A new nest's tracks copy the mute and solo of the tracks they came from, so the selection sounds the same once it's nested. Un-nesting doesn't keep what's set on the nest's tracks.
243	    50	
244	    51	## In an export
245	    52	
246	    53	Mute and solo are part of the project, so the export hears what you hear. A silenced track isn't in the exported mix, and it writes no [stem](/export/stems/). If every track is silenced, Frame Job won't write stems.
247	    54	
248	    55	:::caution
249	    56	A solo left on silences the rest of the export. Check the header switches before you export.
250	    57	:::
251	    58	
252	    59	## Good to know
253	    60	
254	    61	- The switches are plain toggles. <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking one does what a click does, and <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking the header away from its switches [selects the track's clips](/timeline/tracks/#the-track-header).
255	    62	- A [scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/) plays the same mix, so mute and solo silence it too.
256	    63	- The header's other switches are on [The track header](/timeline/tracks/#the-track-header).
257	    64	
258	    65	## Related
259	    66	
260	    67	- [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/)
261	    68	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
262	    69	- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)
263	    70	- [Audio stems](/export/stems/)
264	=== track-volume-and-pan
265	     1	---
266	     2	title: Track volume and pan
267	     3	description: Set a whole track's level and left-right balance in the Track Mix panel, on top of what each clip already does.
268	     4	---
269	     5	
270	     6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
271	     7	
272	     8	Each track has its own volume and pan, applied on top of every clip on it. Use them to balance a music bed against a voice-over without touching each clip.
273	     9	
274	    10	<AtAGlance
275	    11	  menu="Track ▸ Mix…"
276	    12	  where={['The sliders switch in the track header', "Mix… in the track's right-click menu"]}
277	    13	  tools="set_track"
278	    14	/>
279	    15	
280	    16	## Open the Track Mix panel
281	    17	
282	    18	Click the sliders switch, the fifth in the track's header. **Mix…** in the track's right-click menu does the same. **Track ▸ Mix…** opens it for the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track), and has no keyboard shortcut.
283	    19	
284	    20	A small panel opens beside the header, with the track's name at the top. It holds **Volume**, **Pan**, the track's [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/), and **Reset**.
285	    21	
286	    22	There's one panel per timeline, so opening it on another track closes the first. Clicking away closes it, and so does anything that takes its track away: removing the track, undoing it away, or going into or out of a nest.
287	    23	
288	    24	The sliders switch is lit while the track's volume or pan is off its default, or a compressor or limiter is on.
289	    25	
290	    26	## Set a track's volume
291	    27	
292	    28	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
293	    29	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
294	    30	| **Volume** | The track's level, as a slider and a field in dB. Beside them, a read-out shows the level as a percentage, or "Off". | Off (at −60) to +12 dB | 0 dB |
295	    31	
296	    32	The quick picks on the field are −12, −6, −3, 0, +3 and +6 dB. Drag the slider to its left end, or type −60, to turn the track off. A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
297	    33	
298	    34	Track volume multiplies what's on the track. A clip at 200 % on a track at −12 dB plays at −6 dB. A muted track is silent whatever its volume.
299	    35	
300	    36	## Set a track's pan
301	    37	
302	    38	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
303	    39	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
304	    40	| **Pan** | Leans the track's sound left or right, as a slider and a field. | −100 (left) to 100 (right) | 0 |
305	    41	
306	    42	The quick picks are −100, −50, 0, 50 and 100.
307	    43	
308	    44	Pan is a balance, like a [clip's pan](/audio/pan-and-mono/), and keeps the overall loudness steady as it moves. It applies after each clip's own pan, and two pans multiply, so a clip panned left on a track panned left leans further left. It has no effect on a mono source.
309	    45	
310	    46	## Reset the mix
311	    47	
312	    48	**Reset** puts the volume back to 0 dB and the pan to the centre, and turns the track's compressor and limiter off. Inside an open nest, it resets volume and pan only. It's greyed out when there's nothing to reset.
313	    49	
314	    50	Each change is one undo step: a drag, a typed value or a quick pick ("Track Volume", "Track Pan"), or **Reset** ("Reset Track Mix").
315	    51	
316	    52	## Track volume in a nest
317	    53	
318	    54	A clip inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) plays through its own track inside the nest, and through the track the nest clip sits on.
319	    55	
320	    56	- **Nesting from one track keeps its sound.** The nest's copy of that track starts at 0 dB and centre, because the track the nest clip lands on still applies.
321	    57	- **Clips from the selection's other tracks** keep their own track's volume and pan inside the nest, and also get the destination track's.
322	    58	- **Un-nesting** puts the clips back on the timeline's tracks without the nest's track settings.
323	    59	- **Mix to mono on a nest clip** folds everything inside it, so the pans of the tracks inside no longer apply.
324	    60	
325	    61	## What hears track volume
326	    62	
327	    63	Track volume is part of what you hear, so it shows up wherever Frame Job measures the mix, and not where it measures a clip.
328	    64	
329	    65	| Hears it | Doesn't hear it |
330	    66	| --- | --- |
331	    67	| The preview and every export, which sound the same | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
332	    68	| The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) | The [Loudness read-out](/audio/volume/#read-the-level) |
333	    69	| [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) | A clip's [limiter](/audio/limiter/) |
334	    70	
335	    71	So a track turned up can take a limited clip past its ceiling. Use the track's own [limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) to hold what the whole track hands the mix.
336	    72	
337	    73	## Good to know
338	    74	
339	    75	A track's volume and pan are one value for the whole track, and can't change over time. To ride the level, use a clip's [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) or [actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
340	    76	
341	    77	## Related
342	    78	
343	    79	- [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/)
344	    80	- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
345	    81	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
346	    82	- [Pan and Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/)
347	=== track-dynamics
348	     1	---
349	     2	title: Track compressor and limiter
350	     3	description: Compress and limit a track's whole sound, or everything in a nest together, and know where the preview differs from the export.
351	     4	---
352	     5	
353	     6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
354	     7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
355	     8	
356	     9	A track can have its own compressor and limiter, acting on the sound of every clip on it together. This page covers a track's. A clip has its own [compressor](/audio/compressor/) and [limiter](/audio/limiter/).
357	    10	
358	    11	<AtAGlance
359	    12	  menu="Track ▸ Mix…"
360	    13	  where={['The sliders switch in the track header', "Mix… in the track's right-click menu"]}
361	    14	  tools="set_track"
362	    15	/>
363	    16	
364	    17	## Turn on a track's compressor or limiter
365	    18	
366	    19	<Steps>
367	    20	
368	    21	1. Open the [Track Mix panel](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/#open-the-track-mix-panel) for the track.
369	    22	
370	    23	2. Tick **Compressor** or **Limit peaks**, below **Pan**. Each turns on at its defaults, and its rows stop being greyed out.
371	    24	
372	    25	3. Adjust the rows.
373	    26	
374	    27	</Steps>
375	    28	
376	    29	Unticking throws the settings away, so ticking again starts from the defaults. **Reset** at the foot of the panel turns both off, and resets the track's volume and pan too.
377	    30	
378	    31	The header's sliders switch stays lit while either is on.
379	    32	
380	    33	## Where they sit
381	    34	
382	    35	Both act on the track's whole sound: every clip on it, after each clip's own processing, its volume, fades, crossfades and ducking, and after the track's volume and pan. The compressor runs first, then the limiter.
383	    36	
384	    37	A track's compressor and limiter hear the track after its fader. That's the difference from a clip's compressor, which hears the clip before its volume. Turning the track down turns down what reaches them, so a compressor at −20 dB over a track at −6 dB compresses less.
385	    38	
386	    39	## Compressor settings
387	    40	
388	    41	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
389	    42	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
390	    43	| **Compressor** | Turns the track's compressor on. | on, off | off | |
391	    44	| **Threshold** | The level above which it starts turning the track down. | −60 to 0 dB | −18 dB | −30, −24, −18, −12, −6 |
392	    45	| **Ratio** | How strongly it turns down sound above the threshold. | 1 to 20 :1 | 3:1 | 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 8, 20 |
393	    46	| **Attack** | How quickly it reacts. | 0 to 200 ms | 10 ms | 1, 5, 10, 30, 100 ms |
394	    47	| **Release** | How quickly it lets go. | 10 to 2000 ms | 200 ms | 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 ms |
395	    48	| **Makeup** | Gain added afterwards. | 0 to 24 dB | 0 dB | 0, 3, 6, 12 |
396	    49	
397	    50	## Limiter settings
398	    51	
399	    52	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
400	    53	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
401	    54	| **Limit peaks** | Turns the track's limiter on. | on, off | off | |
402	    55	| **Ceiling** | The highest true peak the track may hand the mix. | −24 to 0 dBTP | −1 dBTP | −1, −2, −3, −6 |
403	    56	| **Release** | How quickly the level recovers after a peak. | 1 to 1000 ms | 100 ms | 50, 100, 200, 500 ms |
404	    57	
405	    58	Each control is a slider and a field. A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
406	    59	
407	    60	## Use a track as a nest's bus
408	    61	
409	    62	A [nest's](/editing/nests/) whole mix plays through the track its nest clip sits on, so a compressor or limiter on that track acts on everything inside the nest together. Put a voice's clips in a nest and compress them as one, whatever tracks they're on inside it.
410	    63	
411	    64	A nest's own tracks have no compressor or limiter. Inside an open nest, both sections are greyed out, and their tooltip says "A nest's mix plays through the dynamics of the track that holds it." **Volume**, **Pan** and **Reset** still work there.
412	    65	
413	    66	Nesting a selection doesn't copy a compressor or limiter from the tracks it came from. The track the nest clip lands on keeps its own.
414	    67	
415	    68	## Exact in the export, approximate in the preview
416	    69	
417	    70	An export plays each track with a compressor or limiter through them on its own, before the tracks are mixed. That's exact, and a [stem](/export/stems/) of that track includes them. The [master limiter](/export/loudness/) still runs over the mix afterwards.
418	    71	
419	    72	The preview can only approximate this. Where a track's clips overlap, such as a crossfade or a nest's tracks, the preview plays the track's sound in more than one piece and runs the compressor and limiter on each piece separately. So the pieces can add up past a track limiter's ceiling while you edit, even though the export holds it.
420	    73	
421	    74	While any track has a compressor or limiter, the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) says so in its footer: "The mix as the preview plays it, with track compressors and limiters approximate, before the export's loudness and master limiter."
422	    75	
423	    76	:::tip
424	    77	Judge a track limiter's ceiling on the export, not on the preview's meters.
425	    78	:::
426	    79	
427	    80	## What hears them
428	    81	
429	    82	| Hears them | Doesn't hear them |
430	    83	| --- | --- |
431	    84	| The preview, approximately | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
432	    85	| The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) and the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/), approximately | The [Loudness read-out](/audio/volume/#read-the-level) |
433	    86	| Every export and stem, exactly | [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) |
434	    87	| | A [scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/) |
435	    88	
436	    89	Normalize, the Loudness read-out, Enhance Voice and Match Audio work on the clip itself, before the track.
437	    90	
438	    91	## Good to know
439	    92	
440	    93	- A track's compressor and limiter are one setting for the whole track, and can't change over time. A track has no EQ or other effects.
441	    94	- Each change is one undo step: a tick, a drag or a typed value ("Track Compressor", "Track Limiter"), or **Reset** ("Reset Track Mix").
442	    95	- A track with a limiter plays 3.3 ms later in the preview, and Frame Job places it 3.3 ms earlier to match, so it stays in sync.
443	    96	
444	    97	## Related
445	    98	
446	    99	- [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/)
447	   100	- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
448	   101	- [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)
449	   102	- [The Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/)
450	   103	- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
451	=== scrub-audio
452	     1	---
453	     2	title: Hear a scrub
454	     3	description: Hear the sound under the playhead as you click or drag along the timeline ruler, to find a word or a beat.
455	     4	---
456	     5	
457	     6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
458	     7	
459	     8	When you click or drag along the ruler, you hear the sound under the playhead. Use it to find a word or a beat by ear.
460	     9	
461	    10	<AtAGlance where="Click or drag along the timeline ruler" />
462	    11	
463	    12	## Scrub the sound
464	    13	
465	    14	Drag along the [ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/). Playback pauses first if it was running. Each time the playhead reaches a new frame, Frame Job plays about 80 ms of the mix forward from it, with a 5 ms fade at each end so the pieces don't click.
466	    15	
467	    16	- A click on the ruler plays one piece.
468	    17	- Hold the mouse still and the sound stops within about a tenth of a second.
469	    18	- Let go and it stops.
470	    19	
471	    20	Dragging left plays each piece forwards from the playhead, not backwards, so a word stays recognisable.
472	    21	
473	    22	## What you hear
474	    23	
475	    24	A scrub plays the mix you'd hear in playback: each clip's volume, fades, ducking, pan and mono, each track's volume and pan, mute and solo, and each clip's sound processing.
476	    25	
477	    26	Three things differ from playback:
478	    27	
479	    28	- A clip's compressor, noise reduction and the processing after them start fresh in each piece, so they can sound different from a steady play.
480	    29	- A track's [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) aren't in a scrub.
481	    30	- The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) stays still.
482	    31	
483	    32	## Silence a scrub
484	    33	
485	    34	Scrub audio is always on, with no setting and no key. To silence it, [mute or solo](/audio/mute-and-solo/) tracks, or turn down your Mac's volume.
486	    35	
487	    36	## Good to know
488	    37	
489	    38	- Only a scrub on the ruler is heard. Stepping with <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd>, **Go** in the [Markers list](/timeline/markers/#the-markers-list), and an agent moving the playhead are all silent.
490	    39	- A scrub doesn't use the microphone, so it never asks for that permission.
491	    40	
492	    41	## Related
493	    42	
494	    43	- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
495	    44	- [The level meter](/audio/level-meter/)
496	    45	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)

36://!   Every placement op takes the partner on an unlocked track with the clip
122://! | `insert_clip` | The insert edit: the clip `at` is strictly inside on `track` is split, every unlocked track opens by the media's whole length, then that media lands at `at`. Only the destination track is cut — straddlers elsewhere ride the shift whole — but for a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at the same `at` and its second half paired with the cut clip's (AU-92). A `lut` media is `add_clip`'s `Err`. |
123://! | `overwrite_clip` | The overwrite edit: `[at, at + media length)` is cleared on `track` ALONE — cut at both bounds, the middles removed — and the media lands there. Nothing shifts and no other track is touched but for a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at the same bounds and paired (AU-92); the partner's middle piece stays, unlinked. A `lut` media is `add_clip`'s `Err`. |
124://! | `move_clip` | Shifts the selection by `delta`, clamped so the earliest clip stops at 0; `track` retargets by track-index delta, keeping relative offsets. A linked partner on an unlocked track moves with its clip by the same delta, the clamp at 0 taken over both so a sound lead is kept; only the clips named change track, so a partner keeps its own (spec §11 AU-91). |
125://! | `trim_start` | New start `to`; a media `in` advances by `(to − start) × speed`. Clamped to the source head — snapped UP to a whole frame, so a floored `in / speed` cannot write a sub-frame start (spec §11, D4-5) — and to one frame before the end. `text.words` are rebased by `to − start`, unlike actions: a word stays on its speech (spec §11, W-3). A graphic's `in` advances by `to − start` (no speed, no head bound), never below 0 (G-9). On a ramped clip the speed actions stay in clip time, `in` advances by round(S(to − start)) moving in and at the base rate moving out, and the edge is held at a fitting frame between `to` and the clip's current start, found by bisection on the frame grid (SR-18 (c)). `alone` (false when absent): without it, a linked partner on an unlocked track whose start equals this clip's is trimmed to the same `to` after it, by its own clamps, and a refusal from either is the answer; with it, the clip moves alone — the J-cut (AU-93). |
128://! | `slip` | Slides the source under a fixed clip: `in += delta × speed`, start and duration unchanged, clamped so the window stays inside the media. A `still` moves its `at` instead. A slip the clamps reduce to nothing is an identity; a source with nothing to slip is an `Err`. On a ramped clip the delta is at the base rate, the tail clamp `file − S(D)`, the speed actions unmoved (SR-18 (d)). A linked partner on an unlocked track slips with it, both by the smaller in magnitude of the two clamped amounts (AU-94). |
129://! | `roll` | Moves a hard cut: this clip's start and its predecessor's end both become `to`. The predecessor is the clip on the track ending EXACTLY at this one's start; with none — a gap, or an overlap, whose length is `set_transition_duration`'s — it refuses. Clamped to one frame and to the source available on each side. This clip's `text.words` are rebased by the move (W-3). This clip's `graphic.in` advances by the move as `trim_start`'s does; the predecessor's `length` is untouched (G-9). Ramped clips keep their speed actions: this clip's `in` moves and its edge is held as `trim_start`'s, the predecessor's bound reads S∞ (SR-18). `alone` (false when absent): without it, a linked partner on an unlocked track whose start equals this clip's and which has a hard-cut predecessor of its own is rolled to the same `to` after it (AU-93). |
130://! | `split` | Cuts at project time `at`. With `clips` absent, cuts every clip on an unlocked track that `at` is strictly inside. The second half keeps every `text.words` entry rebased by the cut (a negative start is legal); a second half whose evaluated content has a different token count stores `words: []` instead — a half is a clip the door must accept again (W-3). The first half's words are untouched. A graphic's second half gets `in + (at − start)` and BOTH halves' `length` are pinned to the original's effective length (`length`, or `in + duration` when null) — G-9. On a ramped clip the halves meet at the source read by the cut, `in + round(S(at − start))`, the second half at the rate there; a straddled speed action's first half ends at the solved rate that reads it, its second half at the original end rate, an `ease_in`/`ease_in_out` one lowered to the largest that fits when it would read past the file (SR-18 (e)). A linked partner on an unlocked track is cut too: both cut, the second halves are linked; the partner not cut, it stays linked to the half sharing more of its time, the first on a tie (AU-92). |
131://! | `delete` | Removes the clips; the gaps stay. A picture takes its linked sound on an unlocked track with it; a linked sound half (picture off) named alone goes alone, its picture staying silent (AU-91). |
132://! | `ripple_delete` | Removes, then closes each removed span across every unlocked track. Markers do not move. Each clip's linked partner on an unlocked track is removed too, either half named (AU-91). |
133://! | `ripple_delete_range` | Splits every unlocked clip at both bounds, removes the middles, then closes the hole. A reversed range is the same range. Every shift (this, `ripple_delete`, `ripple_delete_ranges`, `close_gap`, `insert_time`, `add_transition`'s ripple form) moves each moved clip's linked partner on an unlocked track too, and refuses, nothing moved, when that would take a partner below 0: "clip S would start before 0: it leads its linked clip P by N ticks" (AU-91). |
135://! | `lift_range` | `ripple_delete_range` without the close: every unlocked clip is split at both bounds and the middles removed, and nothing moves. A reversed range is the same range. |
136://! | `keep_range` | The project as `[from, to)` of its top-level timeline, moved to start at 0 (spec §11 CJ-50, `edit_keep_range.rs`): both bounds snapped and clamped to 0, `to` not after `from` an `Err`; every clip on every track, locked or not, cut at both bounds by `split`'s rules; at an edge inside a transition the piece beyond the edge is dropped and the incoming piece starting at `from` hard-starts (no `transition_in`), the incoming piece kept when both bounds lie in one overlap; clips not wholly inside removed, the rest and the markers inside moved by −`from`, markers outside removed; nests no kept clip reaches and media no kept clip plays, names in a look or converts through removed; tracks and canvas unchanged. Refused: a nest clip across an edge, nothing left to play, and a transition inside the range whose clip an edge cut too short for it. Document-level, with no tool: it is applied to a derived document only (CJ5b). |
137://! | `insert_time` | Opens a hole: every unlocked clip, and every marker, at or after `at` moves right by `length`. |
138://! | `close_gap` | Closes the empty span on `track` that contains `at`, bounded by the nearest clip edges there: everything from its far side shifts left by its length, across every unlocked track. Refuses on a locked `track`, on an `at` that is on a clip, with no clip after the gap, and when the shift would break the overlap rule — a gap closes fully or not at all. A linked partner of a moved clip moves too, and a partner the shift would take below 0 refuses (AU-91). |
139://! | `retime_range` | Plays `[from, to)` at `rate` on every unlocked track and moves everything after it up or back to stay in step, one undo step (spec §11 CU-90). Both bounds are snapped and clamped to 0; `f(t) = snapped(from + round((t − from) ÷ rate))`. Both bounds are cut by `split_under_playhead`; each piece wholly inside starts at `f(s)` and lasts `f(e) − f(s)`: a constant media piece plays at speed × `rate`, held to its media, a ramped one scales its whole profile by `rate` (SR-19), and a text, shape, still, image, graphic (its `length` kept) or adjustment piece scales its start and duration; actions keep their fraction; `keep_pitch`, when given, is set on each media piece's audio. Everything at or after `to` moves by `to′ − to` with its linked partners (AU-91); markers inside map through `f` and markers after move with the shift (none inside a nest). A `rate` of 1 is an identity. `Err` for a rate that is not a positive number and a `to` not after `from` on the grid. Refused, in this order: a rate past ×0.1–×1000; a range under two frames; a locked track holding a clip that ends after `from`; a nest clip, a caption page with timed words or a linked clip (AU-94) in the range; a transition touching `[from, to]`; two markers landing on one tick; a piece whose rate would pass the speed limits (naming the rate) or that would last under one frame. |
145://! | `duplicate` | Copies each clip one selection-span later on its own track, with fresh ids. A linked partner on an unlocked track is copied too, and the copies are linked to each other (AU-96). |
146://! | `copy_pieces` | Copies `clip`'s pieces between each of `ranges`' project times onto `track` at the same times (spec §11 SW-11, SW-12), each piece exactly the middle a `split` at its two ends would leave, with fresh ids, no transition and no link; `video` and `audio`, when given, set each piece's `enabled`. Each pair is put in order and snapped, a range empty on the grid dropped (none left is an identity), the rest sorted. `Err` for an unknown clip, then track. Refused, in order: a nest clip, a range outside the clip, overlapping ranges (touching is allowed), a locked destination, a destination holding a clip over a range. Allowed inside a nest. |

docs/guide/audio.md:94:- The line shows what this clip contributes, so it moves with the clip's track volume and ducking, but a drag changes only the clip's own level. On a silenced clip the line stays on the floor while the readout changes. Inside an open nes

479:When the shot before was detached too, its sound sits on the same track as this one's, so a lead would overlap it and become a cross dissolve. **Drag the sound to a track of its own first**, then trim it: on its own track, the lead over

docs/guide/audio.md:721:- A linked clip's speed and direction can't change until you attach its audio.

docs/guide/editing.md:68:Hold ⌥ while you drag a media clip's **end** edge to stretch it instead. The clip's speed changes so that the same content fills the new length (undo name "Rate Stretch"). ⌥ on the start edge does an ordinary trim. 
docs/guide/editing.md:106:- If the splits would take the project past 4,096 clips, counting each linked clip they also cut, nothing is split and the inspector says how many clips it would add and how many fit.
docs/guide/editing.md:268:- **A gesture** is one step from mouse-down to mouse-up: a move, trim, rate stretch, slip, roll or duplicate-drag. A click that selects without moving makes no step.
